data.narrative:
Sila Nanotechnologies is a late-stage private company in the Climate & Energy sector that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a peer universe of 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA) and 8 private peers in the sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression methodology was applied, using total capital raised ($1.3B) as a proxy for valuation floor and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage-to-next-stage advancement. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $1.6B. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable: while 8 same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap emerged within narrower filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) to generate a statistically meaningful median, and relying on all-sector data would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a range of $1.3B to $1.8B, with a central estimate of $1.6B. This range reflects the floor anchored to capital deployed and the ceiling implied by stage-typical step-ups, balanced against sector volatility. Key uncertainties include the absence of a tightly-matched peer set for cross-validation, near-term revenue traction and unit economics in battery materials commercialization, and macroeconomic sensitivity within the capital-intensive energy transition market.
